handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.intro:
A simple addon for existing or new Radio Towers, carrying radio signals across tens of thousands of blocks.

Use the arrows to read, or jump to a topic below.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.start.tex:
You will need five things to start up your new radio network:
1) An existing tower
2) A Relay
3) A Repeater Bank
4) A Frequency Card
5) A Catalyst

Attach your new Relay to an existing Simple Radio tower's core. Unlike a Receiver or Transmitter, the Relay does not work on its own. It requires an antenna atop the core, or an antenna connected through wired insulators. Install a Catalyst as well, which sets the maximum strength of relayed transmissions.

Connect a Repeater Bank to the top of your new Relay. While this block does nothing on its own, it is required to process the signals for relaying.

Craft one or more Frequency Cards and tune them at the Radiosmithing Station. Each Repeater Bank allows a Relay to repeat up to six frequencies. Install a tuned Frequency Card into your Repeater Bank, and it's good to go.

Congratulations! You have set up a Simple Radio Relay! Users with transceivers or other Simple Radio devices in receiving range of this tower can now hear signals from users who can transmit to it, even if those users are out of range of each other.

Build more Simple Radio Relay Towers to extend the network even further! Signals lose power over successive hops. Better Catalysts and upgrades can help on larger networks.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.relay.tex:
The Relay block is the core of your new relay network. Place it beside a metal core with an attached antenna to extend your network through the other compatible devices. It has two slots and one connection point.

The Relay requires a Catalyst to function. The standard catalysts are an amethyst block and gilded blackstone. Your choice determines how much of the tower's power this Relay can use to boost transmissions.

With each successive jump across a network, the available boost drops by 10%. A better catalyst means your towers don't need to be as enormous to carry messages across a few extreme-distance jumps.

The optional upgrade slot can improve the Relay's power, counter relay degradation, or add other abilities. See Amplifiers for more details.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.bank.text:
The Repeater Bank lets you select which frequencies your new Relay forwards. Attach it directly to the top of your Relay block to get it working.

Install tuned cards by right-clicking an available front slot. Right-click an inserted card with an empty hand to remove it.

Forwarding multiple signals on a single Relay does not combine those channels; they are all kept separate.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.transpond:
The Transponder is an advanced Relay component. It connects one frequency on the left to up to two on the right, using Simplex, Duplex or Multicast mode.

Install it on top of a Relay instead of a Repeater Bank. Right-click an available front slot to install a Frequency Card; right-click an inserted card with an empty hand to remove it.

The Transponder needs a card on the left (RX) and at least one on the right (TX). Right-click its middle panel to cycle through its three modes.

Simplex (one-way arrow): transmissions received on RX are sent out on the TX channels. Incoming transmissions on the TX channels are not rebroadcast.

Duplex (two-way arrow): RX transmissions are sent to the TX channels. Incoming transmissions on either TX channel are sent back to RX.

Multicast (asterisk): transmissions are shared across all installed RX and TX channels in both directions.

Examples:
Simplex: A user on TX1 or TX2 receives relayed transmissions from users on RX, but not the other TX channel. A user on RX does not hear TX1 or TX2 through this Transponder.
Duplex: A user on TX1 or TX2 receives relayed transmissions from users on RX, but not the other TX channel. A user on RX hears transmissions from TX1 and TX2.
Multicast: Users on all three channels receive each other's transmissions.

These examples describe this Transponder's forwarding. Nearby radios can still hear direct transmissions on their own channel.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.card.text:
Frequency Cards let you tune your relay towers. Without them, nothing is forwarded.

Tune your cards at a Radiosmithing Station, then plug them into a Repeater Bank or Transponder. Match the frequency and AM/FM mode of the devices you want to connect.

Remove, rewrite and reinstall cards whenever you like. Each inserted card shows its frequency for easy identification.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.amplifier:
Several amplifiers are available: basic Copper and Redstone Amplifiers, and the powerful Ender Amplifier.

Install one in a Relay's upgrade slot to increase the relay power rating of the attached antenna.

Ender Amplifiers also reset a signal's relay power degradation. The signal is rebroadcast at the full power available to that Relay, as set by its Catalyst.

This does not restore audio quality lost before reaching the upgraded Relay, but it lets the signal travel further before losing its remaining power.
handbook.simpleradio_repeaters.troublesh:
Make sure your Relay shows READY and a positive ANT value, and that a Catalyst is installed.

You need at least one tuned Frequency Card in a Repeater Bank, or at least one RX card and one TX card in a Transponder.

Being able to talk from near Relay Tower 1 to a receiver near Relay Tower 2 does not guarantee that a signal from further away, such as Tower 5 or 6, can make the same jump.

Improve the antenna, install an amplifier, or build more intermediary Relays to help weaker signals travel further.
